title: Mirai_Botnet_Investigation_82b
description: Investigate unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation in the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation. Your task is to investigate and identify the source of these issues. This training will guide you through identifying suspicious services, analyzing network traffic, and investigating persistence mechanisms to enhance your cybersecurity skills.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external host?
levels.solution:
Check the running services and look for any unusual or unfamiliar services. Pay attention to services that might be communicating with external hosts.

To identify the suspicious service, use the following command:

```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service
```

The suspicious service is `bot-beacon-Hilix.sh.service`. The flag type is a systemd service name.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by understanding the types of services that might be running on the system and how they can communicate externally.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use systemctl commands to list all running services and look for any that are unfamiliar or suspicious. Try the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious service is named `bot-beacon-Hilix.sh.service`. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to find it.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating the abnormal network traffic?
levels.solution:
Investigate the network connections and look for any services that might be sending a high volume of traffic to an external host.

To identify the service generating abnormal network traffic, use the following command:

```bash
ss -tulnp
```

The service generating abnormal network traffic is `bot-flood-Hilix.sh.service`. The flag type is a systemd service name.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand how network connections are established and how to identify services that might be sending excessive traffic.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use network monitoring commands to list all active connections and look for any that are unusual or suspicious. Try the command `ss -tulnp`.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The service generating abnormal network traffic is named `bot-flood-Hilix.sh.service`. Use the command `ss -tulnp` to find it.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution:
Check the systemd services and timers to see how the suspicious service is being started automatically.

To determine the persistence mechanism, use the following command:

```bash
systemctl list-timers
```

The persistence mechanism is a systemd timer named `bot-beacon-Hilix.sh.timer`. The flag type is a systemd timer name.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand how services can be configured to start automatically after a system reboot using systemd.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use systemctl commands to list all timers and look for any that are associated with the suspicious service. Try the command `systemctl list-timers`.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The persistence mechanism is a systemd timer named `bot-beacon-Hilix.sh.timer`. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to find it.
